title: build on arm64-apple-darwin (targetting x86_64-apple-darwin); specify library root for x86
author: Jofkos
body:

I am attempting to build touchHLE from source, on an Aarch64 macOS system, targetting `x86_64-apple-darwin`. It seems to work fine, until it gets to the c++ part – which fails as it is trying to link to the arm64 binaries of certain libraries. This should be an easy fix, by just providing it with the alternate location of the x86 libraries, yet I haven't found a way to do so (it seemed to ignore them).

How do I pass an alternative library root to cargo so that it links against the correct libraries?

comments.author: hikari-no-yume
comments.body: Hi, thanks for testing this! Do you know which libraries the problem happens with? There's several different native builds going on in this project: some using the `cc` crate, some using the `cmake` crate, and then the `sdl2` crate is also building something, not sure how.

comments.author: hikari-no-yume
comments.body:
Re: SDL2, maybe you can edit `Cargo.toml` so we don't use the static linking feature of the crate `sdl2`. That might work as a quick fix. You'll need to get SDL2 on your system by some other means then however, perhaps from Homebrew.

Re: the dynarmic errors, are you using the latest trunk or one of the releases? I think an issue with `std::vector` was fixed on trunk recently, not sure if it's the issue you have.

comments.author: Jofkos
comments.body:
Installing SDL2 as [framework](https://lib.rs/crates/sdl2#readme-if-you-are-using-the-sdl2-framework) and using the `use_mac_framework` feature of the `SDL2` crate seems to do the trick.

I am using the latest trunk, so apparently that fix wasn't it (at least for my use-case).

comments.author: hikari-no-yume
comments.body: It's probably just a missing `#include <vector>` in one of dynarmic's files. Does the latest master version of dynarmic (cd into `vendor/dynarmic`) work? If not, maybe file a bug on their repo, if you want to.

comments.author: Jofkos
comments.body:
Updating `dynarmic` did the trick! Now I am getting a new error, however:
`error: could not find native static library `fmtd`, perhaps an -L flag is missing?`
which seems to occur on Linux too (https://github.com/hikari-no-yume/touchHLE/issues/3#issuecomment-1416187408), Yet the fix proposed there doesn't seem to work.

I also tried setting `dynarmic`'s `CMAKE_DISABLE_FIND_PACKAGE_fmt=on`, bundling `fmt`, but something else is going wrong there:
```bash
  = note: ld: warning: directory not found for option '-L/Users/Jofkos/Developer/touchHLE/target/x86_64-apple-darwin/debug/build/touchHLE_dynarmic_wrapper-e27898037933d9b7/out/lib64'

          ld: library not found for -lfmt
          clang: error: linker command failed with exit code 1 (use -v to see invocation)
```

`dynarmic` itself does compile, when invoking `cmake` with `-DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES="x86_64"` and `-DCMAKE_DISABLE_FIND_PACKAGE_fmt=ON` manually, so if there was a way to pass those flags on to `cmake`, that might be the fix needed.

comments.author: hikari-no-yume
comments.body:
Ah, the `fmtd` thing will probably be related to which paths (specified by `src/cpu/dynarmic_wrapper/build.rs`) are searched for libraries.

Uhh, can you have a look in `/Users/Jofkos/Developer/touchHLE/target/x86_64-apple-darwin/debug/build/touchHLE_dynarmic_wrapper-e27898037933d9b7/out/` and see what the directory structure is like? Presumably there's a `libfmtd.a` file in there somewhere?

comments.author: hikari-no-yume
comments.body: Another possibility is that it's looking for `libfmtd.a` but the library is actually `libfmt.a`. The name is supposed to vary depending on whether it's a debug or release build, but maybe that changed?

arm64 compilation did not work out of the box, and as you only mentioned support for x86, I thought that would be the easiest to do. 🤦

```CMake
set(CMAKE_DISABLE_FIND_PACKAGE_fmt ON)
```
in the dynarmic `CMakeLists.txt` :) 🎉
